newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court allows Chinese couple's extradition.
newsitem.headline: Polish court allows Chinese couple's extradition.

text.p: The Warsaw court of appeals on Friday allowed the extradition of a Chinese couple, wanted by Beijing for embezzlement, dealing a blow to human rights campaigners who argued they might be shot.

The city's provincial court said last month that the couple -- Mandugeqi, 52, and his 42-year-old wife Yinge -- should not be deported to China because they could suffer violations of their human rights there.

But the Polish prosecutors' office appealed against the verdict and PAP news agency said the appeals court on Friday decided that in this particular case there was no reason to believe the couple's rights would be infringed, PAP said.
"It (the lower court's decision) was based on generalised facts about human rights violation in China," PAP quoted the official justification of the verdict as saying.

The couple's attorney said he would submit the case to the Supreme Court. If it backs the court of appeals' ruling, the prosecutor general would still be entitled to let the couple stay in Poland as Warsaw and Beijing do not have an extradition agreement.

Human rights activists have argued that the couple, members of the Mongolian ethnic minority, could face the death penalty often imposed in China for economic crimes, even though Chinese authorities had promised they would not be executed.
On Sunday China's embassy in Warsaw issued a statement condemning the provincial court decision and saying it amounted to protection of criminals.

The couple were detained in Warsaw in August on the basis of an Interpol notice and have since been held in separate jails. Chinese authorities issued an arrest warrant in 1994, the year after they left the country.

Their lawyer Wojciech Hermelinski earlier said the pair faced imprecisely-formulated allegations of fraud, failing to repay borrowed money from banks and individuals and of not paying for goods, together involving a total of about 17.5 million yuan ($2.1 million).

The couple argue they repaid practically all they owed and assets they left in China covered any outstanding sums. They have asked for political asylum in Poland and the application is still being considered.
